{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-sd-x","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"9d2858d1a4f8b84058c3739be588b1f16575d2ed1a6e5a9f72ee2763d7e5284a","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-sd-class-std:lineage:59","source_registry_sha256":"a4e51960bfe4da242ea11046073ac8d3d0353ce120a5409a11c1f9ab4c4da57a","source_liveness_sha256":"1aea607665fc1312b9a6988c94545b32e414886d6d428b2b6d66e4261f9397f1"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Visual search, speed and stopping","heading":"C — Knowledge dossier: Visual search, speed and stopping","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Knowledge dossier: Visual search, speed and stopping

FACT_ID: sec14-F01 | anchor: A48
Use a regular moving visual search ahead, beside and behind the vehicle rather than staring at one area. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-F02 | anchor: A48
Looking far along the intended path gives time to plan speed and position changes and may avoid emergency braking or steering. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-F03 | anchor: A48
Ideally, scan conditions 20 to 30 seconds ahead of the vehicle. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-F04 | anchor: A48
Adjust speed and position to maintain a useful view, avoiding following so close to a large vehicle that sight distance is restricted. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-F05 | anchor: A48
Early observation permits gradual slowing or lane changes that reduce unnecessary braking and fuel use. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-F06 | anchor: A48
Earlier driving adjustments give following drivers more reaction time and help traffic maintain a steadier pace. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-F07 | anchor: A48
Scan both sides before vehicles or pedestrians can cross the path, particularly at intersections and rail crossings. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-F08 | anchor: A48
An intersection includes any traffic merging or crossing point, such as a side street, driveway or parking-area entrance. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-F09 | anchor: A48
Look left and right before entering an intersection and recheck just before moving after a stop. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-F10 | anchor: A48
Before entering, look across the intersection to ensure the route is clear through it and a stop will not block it. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-F11 | anchor: A48
Before a left turn across traffic, choose a safe gap, check the receiving street for vehicles or pedestrians, then recheck oncoming traffic. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-F12 | anchor: A48
Before turning right, check traffic from the left, opposing vehicles turning left and pedestrians in the intended path. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-F13 | anchor: A48
A right turn on red is forbidden when a sign prohibits it. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-F14 | anchor: A48
Check both directions even when other traffic faces red or a stop sign, especially just after your light becomes green. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-F15 | anchor: A48
If the cross-street view remains blocked after stopping, edge forward slowly until crossing traffic becomes visible. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-F16 | anchor: A49
Use mirrors to monitor traffic behind, especially for lane changes, slowing, stopping, intersection entry, backing and long or steep descents. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec14-F17 | anchor: A49
Check rear traffic more frequently in heavy traffic to recognize fast-closing vehicles or close following. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec14-F18 | anchor: A49
Lane-change checks also apply when merging from an entrance ramp or entering from a curb or shoulder. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec14-F19 | anchor: A49
Before changing lanes, use rear and side mirrors to confirm the lane is clear and no vehicle is starting to pass. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec14-F20 | anchor: A49
Physically look over the shoulder toward the intended movement to check near the rear corners that mirrors cannot show. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec14-F21 | anchor: A49
Drivers must signal for turns and lane changes. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec14-F22 | anchor: A49
The handbook requires signaling at least 100 feet before an intersection and advises 4 to 5 seconds of advance signal at higher speeds. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec14-F23 | anchor: A49
Use an electric signal or the left arm and hand to communicate the required signal. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec14-F24 | anchor: A49
Make side and rear checks brief, returning attention ahead because traffic there may stop suddenly. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec14-F25 | anchor: A49
Recheck the blind spot just before the lane change and use several short looks when needed rather than one long look away. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec14-F26 | anchor: A49
Look for motorcycles, bicycles and pedestrians that are harder to see, especially when entering from a curb or driveway. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec14-F27 | anchor: A49
Check behind when slowing, especially during rapid slowing or at a driveway or parking space where it may be unexpected. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec14-F28 | anchor: A49
Minimize reversing when possible, such as by choosing a drive-through parking space that allows forward departure. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec14-F29 | anchor: A49
Before backing, inspect behind the vehicle before entry, then turn to look through the rear window rather than relying on mirrors alone. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec14-F30 | anchor: A49
Back slowly and use an outside helper whenever one is available. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0049]

Misconceptions: A green signal does not prove the intersection is clear; the braking-distance example is not total stopping distance; the baseline following interval must grow in the listed conditions.
Mnemonics: Use look, predict, space and adjust as an authored scanning cue.
Glossary: Perception recognizes the need to stop; reaction moves toward braking; braking distance covers brake action; a space cushion gives room and time to respond.
Dynamic facts: Traffic, visibility, weather and wildlife presence change continuously. Published deer statistics and human-response examples require context rather than personal guarantees.
